newsitem.title: USA: Lawsuit filed to block new NYC bonding authority.
newsitem.headline: Lawsuit filed to block new NYC bonding authority.

text.p: A lawsuit was filed by two New York State residents to block a newly created bonding authority for New York City because they believe it violates the state constitution.
The lawsuit was filed Monday in the Supreme Court in Albany County by taxpayer activists Robert Schulz and Gary Loughrey.
Schulz and Loughrey could not be reached for immediate comment.

The lawsuit against New York City Transitional Finance Authority, a temporary public authority created in Febraury by lawmakers to help the city with its capital needs with up to $7.5 billion of debt, claims that the new entity violates a number of provisions of the state constition for a number of reasons, including lack of voter approval for the bonding authority's debt and violation of mandated city debt limits.

Schulz is no stranger to these types of lawsuits, having filed lawsuits in the past to block other bond authorities that he beleived violated the state constituion. Schulz is currently challenging the state's $1.7 billion environmental bond act, approved by voters in November.

The city is reviewing underwriting firms for the new authority, which would sell debt to finance city projects that would not otherwise be financed with bonds because of a consutituionally mandated debt ceiling on city bond sales. The city is approaching the debt limit and created the new authority to continue financing projects even after the city has hit the ceiling.
City officials were not immediately available for comment. --U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650
